original_question: Let Z be a holomorphic vector field on C2. Can there be one positive-measure set of leaves whose universal covers are C and another positive-measure set of leaves whose universal covers are the unit disc?
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper very closely: it is about a holomorphic vector field on C^2, asks about leaves of the induced foliation, and isolates exactly the coexistence question between leaves uniformized by C and leaves uniformized by the unit disc. Rephrasing "covered by C" as "whose universal covers are C" is mathematically faithful.
missing_details: The paper asks the question for the foliation by Riemann surfaces induced by the holomorphic vector field Z; that foliation should be named explicitly if the question is to stand alone.
The leaves under discussion are the nonsingular leaves of the singular holomorphic foliation induced by Z, i.e. on C^2 \ Z^{-1}(0).

The paper's exact language is "leaves covered by C" and "leaves covered by the unit disc"; a stand-alone version should make explicit that this means the universal covering surfaces are biholomorphic to C and to the unit disc Δ.

The surrounding context is Section 8's transcendental/general holomorphic setting: no polynomiality, degree, homogeneity, nondegeneracy, nilpotency, or 'for sufficiently large m' type hypothesis appears here, so none should be added.
To be fully stand-alone, one would have to specify what measure on the family of leaves is intended by "a set of positive measure of leaves"; the paper itself leaves that measure notion implicit.

The neighboring subproblems 8.1(ii) and 8.1(iii) are different questions (about parabolicity on a non-pluripolar set and sufficient conditions for all leaves to be disc-covered), so they should not be merged into the refined question.

If one wants the nearby terminology, Section 6 defines a parabolic Riemann surface; this explains the relation to the phrase 'covered by C', but the exact target is still the explicit C-versus-disc question in Problem 8.1(i).
refined_question: Let Z be a holomorphic vector field on C^2, and let F_Z be the singular holomorphic foliation by Riemann surfaces induced by Z on C^2 \ Z^{-1}(0). Is it possible that F_Z admits one set of positive measure of leaves whose universal covering surface is biholomorphic to C, and another set of positive measure of leaves whose universal covering surface is biholomorphic to the unit disc Δ?
justification: The draft is targeting the exact open problem stated in Section 8: Problem 8.1(i) asks whether a holomorphic vector field in C^2 can have a positive-measure set of leaves covered by C and another positive-measure set of leaves covered by the unit disc. This is the nearest official formulation and should not be broadened to the neighboring questions in Problem 8.1(ii)-(iii). The opening sentence of Section 8 says that the section studies analogues of results for polynomial vector fields in C^2 in the setting of general holomorphic vector fields, so the refined question should remain in that unrestricted holomorphic/transcendental setting and should not introduce degree or nondegeneracy assumptions. The sentence immediately after Problem 8.1 confirms this by giving the polynomial/non-degenerate case only as background comparison, not as part of the hypothesis. Section 6 supplies the paper's terminology that connects 'covered by C' with parabolic leaves, but the exact target remains the explicit uniformization dichotomy in Problem 8.1(i).
